summary: This file exports a Snippet component that displays code blocks with optional explanations. It supports line-by-line annotations via tooltips, a summary explanation toggle, syntax highlighting for many languages, and proper handling of special characters. The component intelligently chooses between a custom ELI5 renderer (for annotated code) or Docusaurus's standard CodeBlock.

explanations.15: This long comment explains that Prism language grammars must be registered on the shared prismjs module instance before being used, and these imports ensure all supported languages are available upfront rather than depending on load order.
explanations.27: These import statements register additional syntax highlighting grammars with Prism — without them, Prism wouldn't know how to highlight code in those languages.
explanations.55: This function recursively searches through React element children (which can be nested) to find a className like 'language-xyz' and extract the language name, supporting both single elements and arrays of elements.
explanations.63: The regex `/language-(\w+)/` looks for the word 'language-' followed by one or more word characters, and `match[1]` extracts just the language name part.
explanations.84: This object maps various file extensions and language aliases to standardized variant names — for example, both 'js' and 'javascript' map to 'js' so they share styling.
explanations.145: This interface defines the shape of icon metadata: the CSS class to style it, the iconify identifier to fetch the actual icon, and an accessibility label.
explanations.329: This checks if a character code is a control character (like ESC or DEL) — these are invisible but sometimes present in real files, so the code displays them as visible Unicode symbols instead.
explanations.332: This loops through each character in the text, checking if any are control characters, returning early as soon as one is found for efficiency.
explanations.339: If the text has no control characters, return it unchanged; otherwise, loop through and replace each control character with its Unicode 'control picture' equivalent so it's visible in the UI.
explanations.345: This converts a control character code to its Unicode representation: DEL (0x7f) becomes 0x2421, and other control characters become 0x2400 plus their code value.
explanations.365: A ref storing the timeout ID so we can clear it later — without storing it, we'd lose track of the timeout and couldn't cancel it.
explanations.369: This clears any previous timeout before setting a new one, preventing stacked timeouts if the user clicks copy multiple times quickly.
explanations.375: The cleanup function returned here runs when the component unmounts, ensuring any pending timeout is cleared so it doesn't try to setState on an unmounted component.
explanations.387: This ref object maps line numbers (as strings) to their badge button elements, allowing the tooltip positioning code to find the exact screen location of each badge.
explanations.405: This selects the appropriate Prism grammar for syntax highlighting: use the grammar for the specified language, fall back to plaintext, or use clike (C-like) as a last resort.
explanations.414: A trailing newline in the code creates an extra synthetic 'line' with just a newline token — this removes it so line numbers match the eli5 object keys which are 1-based.
explanations.426: getBoundingClientRect() returns the element's position and size relative to the viewport, which we need to position the tooltip directly above the badge.
explanations.428: The tooltip appears at the same vertical position as the badge (`rect.top`), but the CSS will use `translateY(-100%-gap)` to shift it upward above the badge.
explanations.429: Calculate the distance from the right edge of the viewport to the badge's right edge, so the tooltip aligns its right side with the badge's right side.
explanations.445: Adding a capture-phase scroll listener catches scrolls even if inner elements prevent bubbling, and passive:true tells the browser it can optimize since we won't call preventDefault().
explanations.478: Convert the line index (0-based) to a 1-based line number as a string, because the eli5 object uses '1', '2', etc. as keys.
explanations.487: The showControlChars() function replaces any invisible control characters with visible Unicode symbols before displaying them, while the copy button still copies the real bytes.
explanations.496: This ref callback stores the button element in the badgeRefs object under the line number key, so positionTooltip() can retrieve and measure it later.
explanations.535: This is the actual explanation text for the active line, either from the eli5 object or null if no explanation exists.
explanations.537: createPortal() renders the tooltip into document.body instead of the normal render tree, preventing it from being clipped by overflow:hidden ancestors.
explanations.561: useId() generates a unique ID scoped to this component instance, ensuring the contentId doesn't conflict with other summaries on the page.
explanations.565: Set the max-height to the element's scrollHeight (full content height) when open, or '0px' when closed — CSS transition animates between these values.
explanations.635: Try to parse the JSON string; if it fails (malformed JSON), catch the error and return null, allowing the component to degrade gracefully.
explanations.645: Check if eli5summary is a non-empty string; if so, trim whitespace and use it, otherwise set it to null so the summary block won't render.
explanations.656: This determines the language in priority order: explicit prop > language detected in children > language from filename extension > plaintext as default.
explanations.666: Split filename by dots and take the last part (e.g., 'file.tar.gz' -> 'gz'), then look it up in the language map.
explanations.678: The resolve function from the Vars store can substitute template markers like '%%name=default%%' with actual values; this gets it for use below.
explanations.679: If code exists, run variable substitution on it (plain text swap, no visible marker), otherwise keep it as-is.
explanations.685: For children (JSDoc-like elements), substitute variables and wrap each substituted value in a VarToken component so it gets styled with an underline.
explanations.698: Check if eli5 exists and has at least one key — if so, there are line-by-line annotations to render.
explanations.699: Use the ELI5 renderer if there are annotations OR if the code contains control characters (which only ELI5 can display correctly).
explanations.710: Extract just the filename from a path (e.g., '/path/to/Dockerfile' -> 'dockerfile'), converting to lowercase for case-insensitive comparison.
explanations.716: Check if the filename matches any Docker-related patterns — if so, use the docker icon and styling even if the detected language differs.
explanations.732: Determine the styling variant (icon, colors, etc.) in priority order: explicit variant prop > docker detection > docusaurus detection > language-based lookup > fallback to 'none'.
explanations.743: Look up icon info for the variant; if not found, use the 'none' icon so we always have valid icon metadata.
explanations.747: Build the display title in priority order: explicit title prop > filename > language name in capitals > generic 'Snippet' label.
